title: Formalities and substitutes for consideration
summary: A formality can have evidentiary, cautionary, channeling, clarifying, or managerial functions.
notes: The seal’s historical force and its later limits differ from a modern writing used as evidence. The notes compare proposals to enforce written promises, statutory presumptions, and the Pennsylvania written-obligations approach described by the book. A signature does not everywhere eliminate the bargain requirement. Conversely, a writing requirement such as a statute of frauds can limit enforcement even where there is a genuine bargain. The specified jurisdiction and provision matter.
